title: Telecommunications Legislation Amendment (Universal Outdoor Mobile Obligation) Bill 2026
short_title: Telecommunications Legislation Amendment (Universal Outdoor Mobile Obligation) Bill 2026
portfolio: Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

speeches.speaker: Melissa McIntosh
speeches.brief: Moved an amendment to the Telecommunications Legislation Amendment (Universal Outdoor Mobile Obligation) Bill 2025, arguing it lacks certainty, clear obligations, emergency-call requirements and device compatibility safeguards, and seeking referral to the Senate Environment and Communications Legislation Committee. Supported improved regional connectivity but questioned the bill's definitions, enforcement, costs, spectrum arrangements and delivery timetable by the end of 2027.

speeches.speaker: Julie-Ann Campbell
speeches.brief: Supported the Telecommunications Legislation Amendment (Universal Outdoor Mobile Obligation) Bill 2025, which would require Telstra, TPG and Optus to provide baseline outdoor mobile coverage using existing networks and direct-to-device satellite technology, with a default start date of 1 December 2027.

speeches.speaker: Elizabeth Watson-Brown
speeches.brief: Supported the Telecommunications Legislation Amendment (Universal Outdoor Mobile Obligation) Bill 2025 while arguing that privatisation had failed to deliver reliable coverage. Cited poor service in parts of the Brisbane area, the safety consequences during emergencies and outages, and the need for public ownership and newer satellite-based connectivity.

speeches.speaker: Alison Penfold
speeches.brief: Argued that the Telecommunications Legislation Amendment (Universal Outdoor Mobile Obligation) Bill 2025 would modernise telecommunications protections but required deeper scrutiny because coverage, affordability, emergency access, device compatibility and enforceability remained unresolved, particularly in regional Australia.

speeches.speaker: Alice Jordan-Baird
speeches.brief: Argued that the Telecommunications Legislation Amendment (Universal Outdoor Mobile Obligation) Bill 2025 would establish a technology-neutral framework requiring Telstra, Optus and TPG to provide baseline outdoor mobile coverage, initially for voice and SMS, with a proposed default commencement date of 1 December 2027 and ACMA enforcement powers.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Declared that specified telecommunications, therapeutic goods, biosecurity, and wine legislation would stand referred to the Federation Chamber, either immediately or following adjournment of second-reading debates, unless otherwise ordered.

speeches.speaker: Mary Aldred
speeches.brief: Supported the Telecommunications Legislation Amendment (Universal Outdoor Mobile Obligation) Bill 2025 and its stronger consumer safeguards, including registration, enforceable industry codes and penalties rising from $250,000 to $10 million, while highlighting regional black spots, the $3 million commitment for Gippsland areas, disaster communications failures and support for mandatory emergency roaming; the amendment remained unresolved.
